questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student tests if the amount of sugar affects how long a candle burns, keeping candle size the same. What type of variable is 'candle size'?
questions.why: Candle size is kept the same on purpose so it doesn't affect the result — that makes it the controlled variable, not the one being measured or changed.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these roles in the shogunate hierarchy
questions.why: The shogun held real military and political control, daimyo were powerful regional lords below him, samurai served the daimyo as warriors, and peasants were at the bottom of the hierarchy.

questions.subject: Technology
questions.prompt: In the spice rack project, what should a design brief describe first?
questions.why: A design brief should start with the problem to solve — like messy spice storage — before any material or tool choices are made. Jumping straight to materials is a common mistake.

questions.subject: Technology
questions.prompt: Why is timber sanded before applying a finish?
questions.why: Sanding removes rough patches and splinters so the finish (like varnish or paint) goes on evenly instead of catching on bumps.

questions.subject: Japanese
questions.prompt: How do you say '11' yen in Japanese?
questions.why: Juuichi is juu (10) + ichi (1), making 11. Juuni is 12 and juuyon is 14, pairing 10 with different numbers, while ichijuu wrongly reverses the correct word order.

questions.subject: Japanese
questions.why: Sanbyaku means 300 — san (3) + hyaku (hundred). Sen is used for thousands, so 'sanzen' would be 3,000, not sanbyaku.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these parts of a historical explanation from deepest cause to final event
questions.why: The long-term cause (years of heavy taxes) builds resentment, a trigger (the new tax law) sets it off, and the revolt is the final consequence — trigger causes are not the whole explanation on their own.
